macro_context: Full evidence in journal/research/2026-11-05-dossier.md. The S&P fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, the worst day for the majors since April 2025, led by AI hardware (SMH -11.2%, MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%), with no single trigger: data-center limits after the election, Qualcomm's outlook, builder financing and a momentum unwind. All 11 sectors fell, while XLU, XLP and XLC lost under 1% and credit moved little (HYG -0.3%). VIX 27.8-28.2, inverted against VIX3M at 25.5. Forced selling is not finished: Barclays expects about $135B of vol-control futures selling over 24-48 hours, and the S&P closed below GS's 7,544 CTA trigger. October payrolls at 08:30 (+59-65k, unemployment 4.2%) land before the open, so the idea is scored after them. Pre-market earnings include VST, OKLO, WULF. Weekend risk after the exit: Iran and Hormuz. Evidence favors a modest one-session bounce, not a bottom: five-day base rates are coin flips, and the case for standing aside is respectable.

ideas.thesis: After an index crash day, high beta has tended to beat low vol from the next open to the close, and the realistic edge is about +40-90 bp, not the headline. On the 11 days since 2021 when SPY fell 3% or more, SPHB/SPLV rose next open to close 9 times, mean +133 bp, but +81 bp without April 2025; SPY itself averaged +6 bp. On the 39 days SPY fell 2% or more it rose 67% of the time, mean +55 bp. The cases closest to today are better than that but small: SPY down 3% or more after an up day, 7 of 8, +105 bp; SPY down 2% or more with SMH down 5% or more, 10 of 13, +88 bp. One gap in the analogs: none of the 11 came with SPY above its 200-day, as it is now (733.00, 0.8% above); SPY down 2% or more near or above the 200-day was 8 of 11, +44 bp. This fits tonight better than Wednesday's idea in the same pair, whose down-day analogs didn't match an up day. The spread is stretched (1-day -7.0%, 5-day -14.8%, 20-day -23.8%, z50 -2.92, RSI 28) and AAII bears are 48%. The bet is for the session only: close to close the record is 7 of 11, and five days out it is a coin flip. Research and technicals agree high beta is washed out but conflict on timing. Forced selling is unfinished (Barclays about $135B over 24-48 hours; S&P below GS's 7,544 CTA trigger; vol-control funds also sell on a +2% day). Leveraged funds add to whatever the session does at the close (about 38% of SMH's volume per 1%). This regime has also punished the trade: on days the spread fell 2.5% or more since July, the next session rose 9 of 19, mean -11 bp, and with VIX at 25-32 the record is 9 of 17, +5 bp. Retail isn't capitulating cleanly (Vanda's partial-day -$338M single-stock outflow came with buying in TQQQ and SOXL), gross leverage is still about 310%, and builder financing was a cited trigger, so a credit leg can't be ruled out. Confidence stays at 2.
ideas.invalidation: The SPHB/SPLV spread is down more than 2.0% from the open (about 0.9 of its 217 bp open-to-close standard deviation over the last 20 sessions), SPHB trades below 120.00 (-4.1% from Thursday's 125.13 close, about 1.1 ATR), or SPY trades below 715.00 (-2.5%, about 1.7 ATR).
